newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN CENTRAL BANK INJECTS T$35 BLN IN FUND.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN CENTRAL BANK INJECTS T$35 BLN IN FUND.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank, responding to rising money rates on tight liquidity, injected T$35 billion worth of funds into the banking system through open market operations on Tuesday, a central bank official said.
The bank executed a repurchase of negotiable certificates of deposit, treasury bills and government bonds offered by interested financial institutions with a rate of 8.00 percent.
The institutions have the option of repurchasing the NCDs, treasury bills and government bonds between six and 14 days, the official said.
At 0400 GMT, the overnight interbank rate eased to 9.699 percent against Monday's 9.852 close -- but still well above the central bank's previously declared 5.0-5.5 percent target zone.
